messages:
incidents-bot: [ALERT] p99 tail latency spike detected for tenant=fjordpay-prod on route=/v1/chat/stream (streaming stalls). p95 jumped from ~400ms -> ~1.6s, p99 ~2.3s. Few streaming client disconnects. Dashboard: https://dash.internal/redwood/alerts/1934567890 :rotating_light: @maya oncall
maya: ack — I'm on it. which model/route is this hitting? any obvious errors in logs?
dmitri: looks like it's concentrated on a single tenant + small set of replicas. model=redwood/large-2025, route=chat-stream. Noticed each request has repeated prompt blocks (huge prompt size) and multiple tool invocations. sample log snippet:
```
req=tx-9f3c id=fj-772 recv=1934567889 model=large-2025 prompt_size=145k calls=invoke_tool:4 total_tokens=12k
  stack: preproc->invoke_tool(url_fetch)->invoke_tool(data_parse)->invoke_tool(format)->finalize
  trace: waiting-for-next-chunk x3
```
leila: that trace is suspicious — tool fanout 3-4x per request will bloat kv cache and streaming buffer. Also seeing many concurrent requests from same tenant (bursting).
maya: mitigation plan: 1) throttle per-tenant concurrency to 4, 2) re-route fjordpay to a smaller quantized model to reduce per-token compute, 3) temporarily disable streaming for that tenant (fallback to chunked responses) to avoid stall backpressure. I can coordinate with infra to push config. any objections?
dmitri: no objections. I'll push routing change and concurrency limit. running:
```
rdwctl routes set --tenant fjordpay --route chat-stream --model redwood/model-small-quant --max-concurrency 4
rdwctl features set --tenant fjordpay --feature streaming:false
```
maya: go ahead and apply. post the output.
dmitri: applied. configmap updated and rollout triggered:
```
configmap/redwood-tenant-routing updated
deployment/redwood-inference-rollout restarted
```
initial error spike: a handful of 503s as pods restarted, then recovery starting.
leila: metrics: p99 down from 2.3s -> ~480ms in ~60s after change. p95 still elevated (~900ms) due to backlog in worker queues. We should warm caches for the warm model to reduce cold-kv misses.
dmitri: kicking cache warmup for tenant:
```
curl -X POST "https://internal-cache-warmup/tenants/fjordpay" -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}"
# progress: warmed 36/40 contexts, complete
```
after warmup: p95 -> 420ms, p99 -> 470ms, error rate normalized.
maya: looks stable. customer impact summary for comms: brief window (~3-4m) of streaming stalls and elevated tail latency for fjordpay-prod impacting a minority of streaming sessions. Mitigations: throttled concurrency, routed to quantized smaller model, disabled streaming for tenant, warmed caches. Root cause likely a client change that caused repeated tool calls / templated fanout. @carla can you send a short note to the account? include apology and that we've mitigated and opened a follow-up.
carla: drafting now — will send this to the customer and copy: "We observed elevated tail latency on your streaming sessions for ~3 minutes due to unusually large templated prompts that produced repeated tool calls. We applied throttling and routing changes and streaming fallback; your sessions are now stable. Apologies for the disruption — our team will follow up with a postmortem and recommended client-side mitigations."
support-bot: outgoing message queued to fjordpay-prod account thread id=acct-772-2026
dmitri: follow-up action items: 1) add telemetry for tool-invoke count per request + alert if >2, 2) enforce default max tool-call depth at runtime, 3) add per-tenant circuit breaker for streaming output backlog, 4) postmortem owned by @dmitri & @leila. I'll open the PM.
maya: assigning to dmitri + leila for postmortem. tagging in incidents board. :white_check_mark: any other notes? also recommend sending a small credits gesture for the affected window (ops / customer success decide).
leila: I'll capture traces and attach request_ids to the PM. recommend we also add a quick eval to simulate the prompt pattern and ensure quantized model handles it gracefully.
maya: thanks all. clearing pager."
